findings.title: Walkthrough step 2 ("Durable in a fresh clone") does not exercise the durability claim it names, and silently writes a stray store record
findings.description: Step 2 runs `git clone . /tmp/sq-clone`. A local-path clone's `remote.origin.url` is a filesystem path, and `derive_project_id`/`normalize_remote_url` (identity.py:101,131) will happily derive a path-shaped `ProjectId` from it — squadron's own checkout derives `github.com/ecorkran/squadron` from its GitHub remote (per 323's variance set). The clone therefore reads no stored record under the real project id, resolves slice 400 from topology alone, and passes the stated expectation ("same before_sha/after_sha") by accident — proving only criterion 1's fresh-topology claim, not the State Management claim that "a range resolved in one checkout is read by a fresh clone of the same remote." It also writes a second `slice_ranges` record keyed on a path (`sliceranges-{sha256(path)[:12]}`), polluting the user-level store with exactly the filesystem-path-keyed record 320's architecture forbids, and the walkthrough never mentions cleanup. Fix: clone from the configured remote (`git clone "$(git remote get-url origin)"`) so the normalized remote — and thus the `ProjectId` — matches, and use a fast-forward slice in that step, where reading the stored record is load-bearing rather than redundant with topology.

findings.title: Frontmatter `dependencies` omits 323, an unconditional prerequisite
findings.description: The frontmatter lists only `400` and `402`, but the Prerequisites section names **323 (complete)** as an unconditional dependency — `baseline_report`, `compute_delta` and `is_within_floor` are consumed by the audit section (D8, criterion 8) with no conditional path. Sibling slice designs put cross-band prerequisites in frontmatter (400 lists `100, 320`; 402 lists `320, 323`), and dependency-aware batch tooling reads these blocks. Add `- 323`. (401 is correctly excluded: the design makes it a conditional, not a prerequisite, and handles both orderings explicitly.)

findings.title: "The 400 tests pass unchanged" contradicts D5's required-field decision
findings.description: D5 makes `environment_root: Path` a required field with no default, but every existing `AdapterContext(...)` construction site omits it — `take.py:101`, `tests/metrology/snapshot/builders.py:80`, and `tests/metrology/snapshot/test_python_length.py:25` — so each fails pyright until it gains the argument. The Development Approach claim "the 400 tests pass unchanged" (line 389) is true only in the sense that expectations are unchanged; the constructor call sites need a mechanical edit. Rewording prevents an implementer from reading the claim literally during task 4.

findings.title: A revert merge naming the slice number persists as a permanent landing
findings.description: The resolver keys on any first-parent merge whose message matches the slice-number pattern. A revert of a slice's landing (or any merge message incidentally naming the number, e.g. a follow-up referencing it) on the target's first-parent line matches and — because stored landings never change — becomes permanent. The Risk Assessment names the generic consequence ("A wrong landing stays in the store") and offers hand-deletion, but doesn't name the revert-merge trigger or say whether the resolver rejects it (e.g. by checking that the merge's diff touches the slice's files, or by documenting it as accepted). Worth one sentence either way.

findings.title: The "oldest first" landing-list invariant is stated but not enforced
findings.description: The schema comment promises "each list non-empty, oldest first, unique after_sha", but the named validator checks cover only empty lists, duplicate `after_sha`, and `merge_sha`/`method` agreement. Since display order ("reported separately, oldest first") depends on the invariant, sorting at read time or adding a validator check would keep it honest rather than trusting write order.

findings.title: Scope, decisions and boundaries align with the architecture and the slice plan
findings.description: Every criterion the plan assigns (durable ranges, export without touching `.git`, lockfile-gated type counts, identity-match-only comparison with named breaks, noise-floor display with sample sizes, no composite score, unresolved slices at project level only, on-demand boundary snapshots, report commands) maps to a mechanism and a numbered success criterion here. The D3 refinement of "fork against merge" is already anticipated by the architecture's own text ("refined in slice 403, D3"). The 401 interplay is handled for both orderings and matches 401's stated reader-caching behavior. Exclusions actively cut scope (no slice table in `report project`, no review noise floor, no dependency install), and the contract change to `AdapterContext` is sanctioned by 400's own integration contract, which delegates export extension to this slice.

findings.title: Failure modes are enumerated for every new I/O path, and bounded-time behavior is restated with specific values
findings.description: The table covers hang (`run_git` kills at the 30 s `GIT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, verified in git_utils.py), unknown revision, refused tar members, extraction `OSError`, missing landing commits (`git cat-file -e` before `ensure_snapshot`, with surviving landings still reported), concurrent writes (last-write-win, with the recovery consequence stated), and store failures. Unresolved range reasons are data, never treated as empty ranges — the anti-silent-fallback rule. The tool-timeout bound (`metrology.snapshot_tool_timeout_s`, default 600 per 400) and the deliberately unbounded in-process extraction are both stated explicitly rather than left implicit.

findings.title: Declared consumption interfaces all verify against the current code
findings.description: `_find_slice_branch`/`_resolve_fork_point`/`_search_merge_commit` exist with the described reflog and grep semantics (the D2 rejection of `_find_merge_commit`'s `main` fallback matches its actual WARNING-documented behavior); `store.write_snapshot`/`list_snapshots` and `_write_atomic` exist (store.py:160,422,446); `compute_delta(baseline: ProjectBaseline, new_run: AuditRun)` and `is_within_floor`'s three-state `None` semantics match D8 exactly; `baseline_report`'s `(project, commit, prompt_hash)` grouping is what the audit section's "latest run at each boundary under one prompt hash" requires; and 402's contract for 403 (None category = missing, `read_side_mapped` labeling, review-scale severity, project-level rollup for `slice_index is None`) is restated without drift in D8/D9 and criterion 9.
